policy: Phrase evidence is sense/function specific; component-word CEFR levels never substitute for phrase evidence.
Oxford Phrase List and British Council learner materials are independent curriculum cross-checks, not official Council of Europe phrase certification.
CEFR can-do descriptors may support a communicative function without certifying one exact wording.
LINGUA_A0 remains internal Pre-A1 survival scaffolding; external A1/A2 evidence is preserved rather than relabelled as A0.
No phrase is production-approved by this audit alone.

sources.name: Council of Europe CEFR Companion Volume

evidence: Oxford Phrase List: 'Thank you' A1
CEFR A1 online interaction includes standard expressions of thanks/apology
records.rationale: High-value survival politeness may be introduced in LINGUA A0 while retaining external A1-oriented evidence.

evidence: Oxford Phrase List: 'excuse me' A1
records.rationale: Appropriate survival-language bootstrap, but not an external A0 claim.

evidence: CEFR A1 describes familiar everyday/basic phrases for concrete needs; exact token-level CEFR certification is not available
records.rationale: Keep as first-party politeness scaffold; do not infer an official phrase level from component-word data.

evidence: CEFR Asking for clarification A1: can express simply that they do not understand
British Council learner examples use 'I don't understand' as a repair expression
records.rationale: The communicative function is explicitly A1-supported; LINGUA A0 use is intentional survival scaffolding.

evidence: CEFR Asking for clarification A2: can ask very simply for repetition when not understanding
records.rationale: Repetition-request function is externally supported but later than LINGUA's internal bootstrap. Exact wording remains first-party.

evidence: Oxford Phrase List: 'How much ...?' A1

CEFR A1 allows asking/answering simple personal/local questions when interlocutor supports interaction

evidence: Oxford Phrase List: 'would like' A1
British Council A1 restaurant reading repeatedly models 'would like'
records.rationale: Independent phrase-level and learner-material evidence support A1.

records.rationale: Exact question phrase is used in A1-oriented material. This is the actual starter-pack key; it replaces the erroneous audit-only key 'phrase:because-simple-reason'.
